name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Micah Lasher's large fundraising and outside spending advantage
Open seat after Jerry Nadler's retirement
model.rationale: The district's +33 Democratic lean makes a Republican win implausible, and Lasher's $3.3 million raised plus $10.8 million in outside support dwarfs Shinkle's $155,000. Markets price Democrats at 98%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or a collapse in Democratic turnout in a low-profile open seat could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Manhattan-based open seat is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of about +33. Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves the seat open, but the party holding it faces no serious structural threat. Micah Lasher has raised $3.3 million and benefits from roughly $10.8 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000 with no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets give Democrats a 98% chance of holding the seat, and no general-election polls or expert ratings exist to contradict the fundamentals. The forecast expects a Democratic win by roughly 29 points, with uncertainty driven mainly by turnout in a race receiving little attention.
